header: Date: 2025-06-04 | Time: 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Samantha Li (Aurelia Head of ML), Ravi Patel (Aurelia Infra Lead), Kelsey Morgan (Aurelia PM)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest benchmark runs comparing Redwood POC setup vs customer baseline (VendorX/OpenAI mixed). Discussed latency P50/P95, throughput, tuning (batching, quantization), and next steps to run dedicated pool tests. Agreement to share logs and schedule infra deep-dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you. Well run about 40 minutes, go over the benchmark sheets, and figure next steps. Samantha, you want to kick off with any context?
[00:18] Samantha Li: Yeah, thanks Jamie. Were mostly interested in P95 for our chat assistant, current baseline right now is VendorX deployed via their hosted endpoint, P95 at about 1.1s on short prompts and around 1.8s on 2k token context, throughput about 18 tokens/sec in our steady test. We want to see if Redwood can meet sub-1s P95 on our 512 token median and scale throughput with batching.
[00:42] Carlos Mendez: Got it, thanks. Quick note, some of our earlier runs used a slightly different prompt prefix so I re-ran with the canonical prompt set you shared. The spreadsheet I uploaded has three tabs: raw runs, aggregated percentiles, and config. Jamie I sent a link in chat.
[01:05] Jamie Park: Yup saw that. Quick housekeeping, the runs labeled run-Redwood-quant32 used int8 quant in the model path, and the baseline tab is what you guys provided from VendorX. There may be small env diffs so we tried to match sequence lengths and batch mix.
[01:27] Ravi Patel: One question though, in the baseline we use a proxy that truncates long headers, could that skew latency? We have corporate egress via a shared proxy and sometimes that adds 80 to 120ms.
[01:40] Carlos Mendez: Yeah proxies will add variance, we put an annotation on runs where the proxy was in the path. For the Redwood-hosted vs dedicated tests we can run without the proxy to isolate the inference delta.
[01:55] Kelsey Morgan: On success criteria, were aiming for P95 under 1.0s for 512 tokens and throughput >=25 tokens/sec for batched QPS. Also cost targets but well do cost after latency is validated.
[02:10] Jamie Park: Great. Ok lets walk the numbers. Carlos can you summarize the P50/P95 table?
[02:18] Carlos Mendez: Sure. So for the canonical 512 token set: VendorX baseline P50 0.45s, P95 1.12s. Redwood POC on hosted (non-quant) P50 0.32s, P95 0.95s. Redwood quantized run (int8-ish) P50 0.29s, P95 0.88s. For 2k token runs baseline P95 1.8s, Redwood non-quant P95 1.4s, quant P95 1.2s. Throughput under batched tests: baseline about 18 tokens/sec, Redwood hosted 26 tokens/sec, dedicated-config test 34 tokens/sec. Caveat: dedicated numbers are from our internal equivalent hardware (2x A10/T4 mix) not yet on your exact infra.
[03:05] Samantha Li: Those numbers look promising, especially quant. Any changes to output quality with quantization? We cant have hallucination regressions.
[03:15] Carlos Mendez: Good call. We ran a sample eval set you provided; quality delta measured via your BLEU-ish score and human spot-checks was within margin, no major semantic regressions on the sampled prompts. We flagged a few edge cases where tokens were slightly different in spacing/punctuation, likely tokenization differences.
[03:40] Jamie Park: To add, our Optimize team also runs eval thresholds and we can set automatic rollback if quality metric drops X%. Well share the eval harness.
[03:50] Ravi Patel: On the dedicated config, you mentioned autoscaling and burst. Can we get deterministic throughput for peak hours? We need predictability.
[03:59] Carlos Mendez: Absolutely, Dedicated offers reserved pools and autoscale policies; you can set minimum replica counts and burst capacity. For deterministic throughput you reserve capacity to match peak and use our routing to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[04:15] Kelsey Morgan: Network again — if we move to private deployment or VPC you support on-prem or VPC peering? Any compliance impacts?
[04:24] Jamie Park: Yes private deployment available, plus VPC connectors and on-prem package for air-gapped. We also integrate with KMS/HSM, SOC2 audits, and can generate audit logs. Well share the security pack.
[04:35] Samantha Li: Good. Back to the numbers, can you explain the test configs that gave 34 tokens/sec? Was that large batch sizes?
[04:43] Carlos Mendez: That was a combination of 1) batch size 8 for short prompts, 2) prefix KV caching enabled for repeated context, and 3) our optimized kernel path for attention with shorter effective sequence. We also disabled tail-latency smoothing in that run so P95 improved but P99 had more variance.
[05:05] Ravi Patel: Is KV cache available in the hosted flow? Wed like to reuse convo context.
[05:12] Carlos Mendez: Yes, KV cache and prefix caching are supported. In hosted its enabled with sticky sessions and our API exposes tokens saved per session. In Dedicated you get more fine-grained cache control. Note: transcription heres a small typo in our earlier notes where KV was transcribed as kayvee, so ignore that.
[05:32] Kelsey Morgan: Any regressions observed vs baseline on long tail prompts? The 2k token delta still matters.
[05:38] Carlos Mendez: For extreme long tail we saw Redwood P95 about 300ms better than baseline in our env, but we think some of that is kernel selection and memory layout. If you have specific long-tail prompts send them and we can run targeted runs.
[05:52] Samantha Li: Yes will send 10 representative long-tail prompts. Also want to ensure metrics capture tail latency and token billing differences.
[06:00] Jamie Park: Noted. Next, quality vs quantization: were comfortable that int8 gives ~10-15% faster inference with minimal quality delta on your eval. We'll share exact examples where outputs differ.
[06:14] Samantha Li: Okay. Regarding the dedicated pool spin up, whats the lead time and cost? We need a ballpark for a 2-3 week pilot.
[06:22] Carlos Mendez: Lead time is typically 2-3 business days to provision a reserved pool in our Dedicated offering. For a 2-3 week pilot we can do a short-term commit with a discounted pilot rate. Jamie will share pilot pricing.
[06:35] Ravi Patel: Also any special infra requirements? We have strict egress and internal NAT routing.
[06:41] Jamie Park: Well need to coordinate with your infra team to confirm ports and VPC endpoints. Carlos will produce a runbook with commands and docker tags used.
[06:52] Carlos Mendez: I noted we saw one noisy run where the proxy added ~120ms; Ill mark runs that included proxy and rerun them without proxy to give a clean comparison.
[07:02] Kelsey Morgan: Can Redwood produce a combined sheet that normalizes for proxy and sequence length so we can present to execs?
[07:09] Jamie Park: Yes, thats the plan. Well produce a normalized comparison and include confidence intervals.
[07:16] Samantha Li: Two more quick items: security questionnaire — when can we expect answers? And also SSO for non-engineering users.
[07:24] Jamie Park: Security pack goes out today, and on SSO we support SAML/SSO and RBAC. Well include setup notes.
[07:33] Samantha Li: Great. Anything else on tuning?
[07:36] Carlos Mendez: One tuning tip — lower batch latency by using adaptive batching with a max wait threshold; it keeps P95 low while still improving throughput. Also experiment with sequence bucketing to avoid padding overhead.
[07:51] Ravi Patel: OK thanks. Can we lock a deep-dive time now?
[07:55] Jamie Park: Carlos and Ravi, we have open slots Wed and Thurs this week, Jamie to follow up in chat—
[08:01] Samantha Li: Wed works for us.
[08:04] Jamie Park: Perfect. Quick recap of next steps: Jamie will share updated benchmarks and security pack; Carlos will share runbook and re-run proxy-less tests; Ravi to confirm proxy/NAT constraints; Samantha to send long-tail prompts and final success criteria. Well aim to run dedicated pool test the week of 6/9.
[08:23] Kelsey Morgan: Thanks all, this was helpful.
[08:26] Jamie Park: Thanks everyone, well send follow-ups and action items. Bye.

Note: transcription may contain small mis-hearings (e.g., sammell for SAML, kayvee for KV). Link shared: https://redwood-internal.s3/aur-poc/benchmarks-2025-06-04.xlsx (spreadsheet), security pack link: https://redwood-internal.s3/security-pack-Aurelia-2025.pdf
